title: Add VPC control plane Terraform module: multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, and Route53 delegation
author: Priya Raman
description: Adds a new Terraform module and higher-level composition for provisioning the VPC control plane used by Redwood Private deployments. Motivation: provide a repeatable, auditable multi-AZ network topology for the control plane with interface endpoints, security groups, VPC peering for customer VPCs, and Route53 private hosted zone delegation to satisfy cross-account DNS resolution. This is required for upcoming private installer automation and to reduce manual post-provisioning steps. What this PR does: 1) New module 'vpc-control-plane' with submodules for subnets (public/private), NAT gateways, route tables, and multi-AZ placement; 2) Interface endpoints for SSM, EC2 messages, and KMS in the control plane VPC; 3) Security group templates and least-privileged ingress rules for control plane components and cross-VPC peering; 4) Automated VPC peering resource with option for shared-services account or customer account peering, including route propagation and route table updates; 5) Route53 private hosted zone delegation support and conditional association with customer VPCs; 6) Example composition in 'examples/private-control-plane' showing usage with variables for CIDR planning and naming; 7) Integration tests (terraform/ci) and documentation updates. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module with inputs/outputs documented - [x] Default CIDR and AZ-aware layouts - [x] Endpoint and SG templates - [x] Route53 delegation & IAM policy snippets - [x] Example composition and upgrade notes - [x] CI plan/apply tests updated Notes on compatibility and upgrade: This module is additive and defaults to creating a dedicated control plane VPC. For existing private installations, follow the upgrade notes in docs/PRIVATE_DEPLOYMENT_UPGRADES.md which cover peering handoff and DNS delegation steps. Backwards-compatible by default but operators should read the notes before flipping delegation variables. Related: ENG-4589 (control plane automation), SUP-1204 (customer reported DNS resolution failures during onboarding).
commits: Add subnet and route table composition with multi-AZ support
VPC peering resource and route propagation logic
Add examples and docs, CI tests for plan/apply
Fix: tighten SG egress rules and add explicit IAM policy for delegation
Address reviewer comments: variable naming and doc clarifications
changed_file_snippets: modules/vpc-control-plane/security_groups.tf: allow only control plane ALB CIDR ingress on 443, no 0.0.0.0/0 SSH
modules/vpc-control-plane/peering.tf: aws_vpc_peering_connection with auto_accept optional and route table attachments when peer_account_id provided
route53_delegation.tf: creates aws_route53_private_zone and aws_route53_vpc_association, adds delegation NS records to management zone
review_comments: Ethan Cole: Please ensure the peering implementation supports cross-account peering without requiring console steps. Also add tests that assert route table updates in at least one AZ.
Priya Raman (author): Added auto-accept toggle and documented the cross-account IAM flow; added CI plan that validates route table entries in the example composition.

María Fernández: Security teams wanted explicit denied ingress for SSH and a short justification in the docs. Please include a migration note for existing SGs so operators don't accidentally open access.
Priya Raman (author): Tightened SG rules and added PRIVATE_DEPLOYMENT_UPGRADES.md with explicit migration steps and example terraform state trick for handoffs.
Jason Liu: Can we add a feature flag to keep Route53 delegation opt-in? I don't want accidental changes to customer's DNS during upgrades.
Priya Raman (author): Added variable route53_delegation_enabled (default = false). Called out in docs and example.
release_notes: New terraform module 'vpc-control-plane' for provisioning multi-AZ control plane VPCs with endpoints, security groups, VPC peering, and Route53 delegation. Defaults are non-destructive; Route53 delegation is opt-in. See docs/PRIVATE_DEPLOYMENT_UPGRADES.md for upgrade steps.
notes_for_oncall: This change modifies peering and DNS delegation paths. On-call should watch the private-deployments DNS resolution alert (net.dns.private-resolve) for 24 hours after rolling upstream control plane changes. If issues appear, rollback via terraform destroy of the delegation resources and re-establish manual delegation per docs.
testing_notes: CI includes plan/apply validation using a 3-AZ example VPC and asserts endpoint creation, security group rules, peering resource presence, and Route53 VPC associations. Manual verification steps documented for operators in PRIVATE_DEPLOYMENT_UPGRADES.md.
changelog_entry: Added vpc-control-plane terraform module (multi-AZ subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53 delegation). Opt-in DNS delegation. (PR #158934)
